title: Risk-Based Internal Audit
overview: Internal auditing is defined by the Institute of Internal Auditors as an independent, objective assurance and consulting activity designed to add value and improve an organization’s operations. By employing a systematic, disciplined approach, it enhances the effectiveness of risk management, control, and governance processes, enabling organizations to achieve their objectives.

With increasing regulatory requirements and heightened stakeholder expectations, the internal audit function plays a critical role in corporate governance. This course, Risk-Based Internal Audit, provides participants with the knowledge and tools necessary to conduct audits aligned with organizational strategies. The course emphasizes efficient, flexible, and results-oriented practices to enhance sustainability and tackle future challenges.
audience: This course is ideal for professionals with some auditing experience, junior auditors, finance personnel, and individuals from other departments seeking to develop best practices in internal auditing. It is also suitable for supervisors and managers looking to enhance or refresh their internal audit knowledge.
methodology: The course employs interactive methods such as expert-led presentations, practical case studies, live demonstrations of sampling techniques, and group exercises to ensure a hands-on learning experience.
objectivesIntro: By the end of the course, participants will be able to:
objectives: Understand the scope, purpose, and function of internal auditing within organizations.
Explain the concept of risk-based internal auditing and its application.
Identify and apply internal audit standards as part of the audit framework.
Differentiate between operational, compliance, and financial audit assignments.
Use fieldwork guidelines and techniques to identify risks, evaluate controls, and conduct controls testing.
Select and utilize suitable internal audit tools, evaluating their pros and cons.
Apply effective sampling techniques, determining appropriate sample sizes and methods.
Detect and respond to fraud, understanding the auditor’s responsibilities in such cases.
